**TrackFlow** is a keyboard-driven roster and contact manager for **track and field head and assistant coaches**. TrackFlow v1.4 stores athlete names, age categories, contact details, addresses, and remarks locally. Coaches can add, edit, search, filter, sort, tag, and delete athletes using short text commands.

While it has a Graphical User Interface (GUI), most user interactions occur using a Command Line Interface (CLI). It is strictly optimized for touch-typist coaches working at a desk between practices and meets who strongly prefer rapid, keyboard-driven text entry over navigating nested GUI drop-downs and bloated sports-management web platforms.
* **Command autocomplete**: Real-time dropdown suggestions for commands and incremental prefix completion using `Tab` to guide rapid, error-free command entry.
* **Age-category filtering**: Use `filter a/AGE_CATEGORY` (e.g., `filter a/Under 14`) to filter athletes by competition category; `list` restores the full roster.

* **Flexible athlete search**: Search partial keywords broadly across all athlete fields (name, age category, phone, email, address, remark, and track events) or target specific fields with prefixes (e.g., `find ave`, `find n/avery`, `find a/Under 14`, `find t/100m`, or `find r/injured`).
* **Multi-field sorting**: Sort the displayed roster by name, age category, phone, email, or address in ascending or descending order (e.g., `sort age desc`).
* **Athlete remarks**: Attach coach notes, status updates, or medical flags directly to athlete profiles with `remark INDEX r/REMARK`.

* **Track event tags**: Maintain athletes' track event specializations using `tag INDEX t/EVENT [t/EVENT]...` and `untag INDEX t/EVENT [t/EVENT]...` (e.g., `tag 1 t/100m t/Long Jump`); locate athletes by event with `find t/EVENT`.

When restoring the window, `MainWindow` reads the saved size and position from `GuiSettings` and asks the
stateless `WindowPlacement` utility, through a static call, whether that position is still reachable on a
connected screen; it keeps no `WindowPlacement` instance. An unreachable position falls back to a size capped to
the primary screen. On exit, `MainWindow` writes the current bounds back to `GuiSettings`.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. `MainWindow` uses the static `WindowPlacement.fit` helper to fit saved outer bounds, including decorations, inside
the visual bounds of a connected screen. A reachable saved position selects the screen with the largest overlap;
an unreachable position falls back to the primary screen's center. Both restoration paths cap dimensions and
clamp coordinates. The preferred minimum is 450 by 400 pixels, limited by the selected screen's usable area.
Normal bounds are remembered in preferences in memory as the window moves or resizes, allowing normal bounds to
survive maximized, minimized, full-screen and OS quit paths. Preference storage writes them on shutdown.
The roster can shrink and scroll independently of the input and footer; command execution does not resize the stage.
`HelpWindow` uses the same fitting helper with its own 480 by 320 minimum, starts on its owner's screen, and
retains later user placement within the session.

This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.
`TrackFlowParser` treats command words without considering letter case and routes commands with parameters to their
dedicated parsers. Its initial matcher accepts line breaks in arguments; the entire submission is still parsed as one
command, not a batch. Each field keeps its existing validation rules. The JavaFX command box is a single-line
`TextField` that removes pasted tabs and line breaks before parsing; users should paste commands on one line with
spaces. Parser-level tests exercise multiline input directly.
`ArgumentTokenizer` recognizes supported parameter prefixes without considering letter case at the start of the
arguments or after `Character.isWhitespace` characters, storing them under their canonical prefix.
`ParserUtil.verifyNoUnknownPrefixes` uses the same boundary to reject unsupported parameter-like tokens of the
reserved single-letter or `addr/` form before values are parsed. For example, unsupported `t/` produces a
command-specific error. Longer slash-containing words such as `wrong/value` remain text.
An extra slash marks literal parameter-like text, such as `A//B` or `r//relay`. Both prefix detection and
unknown-prefix validation skip slash-terminated prefixes followed by another slash. After splitting arguments, the
tokenizer strips surrounding whitespace and removes exactly one slash from a run of at least two slashes after a
single-letter or `addr` token. Decoding happens once, including in the broad-search preamble, so decoded text cannot
introduce new arguments. `A///B` becomes `A//B`, not `A/B`. URLs, network paths, quotation marks, and backslashes
are not special syntax. Escaped tokens cannot supply required fields or bypass ordinary field validation.
A slash-led value must be separated from its real prefix by whitespace: `addr/ /home/coach` supplies the address
`/home/coach`, while `addr//home/coach` is literal text and does not introduce an address parameter.
Commands that take no arguments (`clear`, `help`, and `exit`) reject extra text. `remark` requires exactly one `r/`
prefix. Index parsing scans ASCII digits once, capping the accumulated value at `Integer.MAX_VALUE` without building
an arbitrary-precision number. It continues validating the remaining characters after reaching the cap, so an
oversized number followed by text is still rejected. Leading zeroes are accepted; all-zero and malformed indexes are
rejected. Oversized positive numbers reach the command's normal invalid-displayed-index check.
`TrackFlowParser` dispatches `find` to `FindCommandParser`. The parser recognizes broad preamble keywords and
`n/`, `a/`, `p/`, `e/`, `addr/`, `r/`, and `t/` criteria. Broad keywords must precede the first field prefix.
Unknown reserved prefixes, duplicate field prefixes, empty field values, and an empty search are rejected before
the model is changed. `ArgumentTokenizer` decodes escaped prefix-like text once, before predicate construction.
`PersonContainsKeywordsPredicate` combines the two groups as follows:
* **Broad keywords:** any keyword may occur in any searchable field (OR).
* **Scoped fields:** every supplied field must match its own value (AND). Each prefixed value is one phrase;
`find n/Avery Tan` does not behave like the two broad keywords in `find Avery Tan`.
* **Both groups present:** an athlete matches a broad keyword OR satisfies all supplied field criteria.
* **No criteria:** matches no athletes. The nonempty-field guard prevents an empty `allMatch` from making a broad
Matching is case-insensitive substring matching. Thus `find n/avery a/Under 14` requires both the name and category,
while `find Blake n/avery a/Under 14` additionally includes athletes matching the broad keyword `Blake`.
`find t/100m` also matches an event such as `4x100m`; exact-event matching is not implemented. Event names are joined
with line breaks, which keeps ordinary single-line keywords from spanning two names.
`FindCommand` replaces the active predicate through `Model.updateFilteredPersonList`. It searches the full roster,
preserves the active sort, and starts displayed indexes at 1. Consecutive `find` commands do not narrow earlier
results: put all required fields in one command. `find` and `filter` replace one another; `list` removes the filter.
None of these view changes saves the roster.
**Design choices:** broad OR matching helps when the relevant field is unknown; AND between named fields allows
precise searches without adding another command. Substring matching supports partial names, contacts and events,
with the tradeoff that short terms can produce extra matches. `filter` remains the exact age-category operation.
The command autocomplete feature is facilitated by `CommandBox` and `AutocompleteEngine`.
It provides real-time dropdown suggestions for commands based on the user's input, and an intelligent prefix insertion mechanism to guide the user in completing complex commands.
* `AutocompleteEngine` stores a predefined list of command templates (e.g., `"add n/ a/ p/ e/ addr/"`, `"edit INDEX n/ a/ p/ e/ addr/"`, `"delete INDEX"`, `"remark INDEX r/"`).

* `CommandBox` listens to changes in the `TextField`'s `textProperty`. While typing an initial command word, it queries `AutocompleteEngine#getSuggestions` for matching templates (matching case-insensitively) and displays them using a JavaFX `Popup` containing a `ListView`. Once whitespace or parameters are entered, or if there are no matches, the popup is hidden.

* **Selection:** When the user selects a suggestion (via Mouse Click or `Tab`), `CommandBox` inserts the command word followed by a space (e.g., `add `), positions the caret, and hides the popup. This leaves space for the user to insert an index or parameters if required.

* **Separation of Selection and Execution:** Pressing `Enter` does **not** select or apply autocomplete suggestions. If the user presses `Enter` while the suggestion dropdown is visible, `CommandBox` hides the popup and executes the command as typed in the text field. This prevents accidental template insertions when a fast typist intends to submit their input.

* **Incremental Prefix Insertion:** If the user presses `Tab` while the suggestion dropdown is closed (or after selecting a command), `CommandBox` uses `AutocompleteEngine#getNextPrefix` to scan the current input and append the next missing prefix based on the command's template. Existing prefixes are matched case-insensitively and regardless of order, allowing the user to construct the command sequentially by pressing `Tab` after entering each parameter's data.
Prefix completion uses `ArgumentTokenizer` so escaped literal tokens do not count as supplied parameters.
* **Aspect: Suggestion selection key (`Tab` only vs `Tab` and `Enter`)**
* **Alternative 1:** Allow both `Tab` and `Enter` to select suggestions.
* Pros: Familiar to users accustomed to web search bars that accept suggestions on `Enter`.
* Cons: Interferes with command execution. A fast typist who types a command and presses `Enter` may accidentally apply an unwanted suggestion template instead of executing what they typed.
* **Alternative 2 (Current Choice):** Use `Tab` exclusively to select suggestions and insert prefixes; reserve `Enter` strictly for command execution.

| Component | Base colour macro | Interface background macro |

Members are hidden by default. Use `show members` or a targeted command such as `show Parser members` after

* Use current Java class names and signatures. A partial diagram may omit unrelated classes, attributes, or
operations; identify its scope in a legend or the DG. Remove obsolete names and visible placeholder classes.
* Show interfaces with `<<interface>>` and a dashed realization line ending in a hollow triangle at the interface.
Use a solid line with a hollow triangle pointing to the superclass for class inheritance.
* Mark abstract classes with `{abstract}` or italics, and mark abstract operations with PlantUML's `{abstract}`
modifier. Use `{static}` for class-level members so that they render underlined. Use `+`, `-`, `#`, and `~`
for public, private, protected, and package visibility. Keep attributes and operations in their respective compartments.
* Use the dashed type-parameter box for generics. It may extend above the class box; that is intentional UML notation.
Keep its text and border visible, with enough space to avoid covering the class name or `<<interface>>` label.
Do not disable it with `genericDisplay old`.
* Use solid associations for retained instance references and dashed dependencies for temporary use or creation.
Mark creation dependencies with `<<create>>` when useful. Show an association as a line or an attribute, not both.
* Put multiplicities at the association ends they describe. Omit them when they are outside the diagram's scope;
an omitted multiplicity is unspecified. Do not add multiplicities to inheritance or dependency arrows.
* Reserve a filled diamond at the whole for a justified whole-part composition. Construction or a `final` field
alone does not establish composition. A hollow diamond denotes aggregation; use an ordinary association when
a stronger whole-part meaning is not justified.
* Package boxes group the classes in the labelled package or component view. A referenced class may sit outside
the box when it belongs elsewhere, such as `EditCommand` outside the parsing package. State any simplified grouping.
* Distinguish `objectName:ClassName` or `:ClassName` participants from class-level participants labelled `<<class>>`
for static calls. Use solid arrows for calls and dashed arrows for replies.
* Show activation bars while participants execute, including the caller while it waits for a synchronous call.
Start a created object's lifeline at its creation message and end each depicted activation consistently with
the return of control. Do not extend an activation through unrelated later calls.
* Return labels must describe actual returned values. Leave void replies unlabelled; constructor replies may also
omit a label. Do not use a reply label to invent a status value for a method that returns `void`.
* Show destruction only when it occurs in the scenario. A local variable going out of scope does not establish
that its object is destroyed. Explain partial traces, abbreviated arguments, omitted calls, and error paths in
notes or adjacent DG text. Use guarded `alt`, `opt`, and `loop` frames for depicted branches or repetitions.
* A horizontal message may cross other lifelines on its way to the receiver. Keep its arrowhead, label, and
destination clear; these crossings do not represent additional calls to the intermediate participants.
* Preserve literal command text in the rendered image. Escape formatting characters when needed, and verify that
examples such as `A//B` still show both input slashes while the decoded result shows `A/B`.
* Arrange related classes in clear rows or columns. Reduce crossings and avoid lines passing through class boxes
or labels. Remove redundant dependency arrows when signatures already convey the information and the diagram
remains clear. Keep meaningful structural associations and explain the scope of any partial view.
* Use local layout hints where needed. The current class diagrams use `skinparam linetype polyline` and
`skinparam ArrowFontStyle plain`. Hidden PlantUML links may constrain spacing or ordering, but must not introduce
visible relationships or placeholder classes. Do not change a relationship's meaning to improve its position.
* Keep detailed explanations in the DG and use compact legends for diagram scope. Folded-corner notes may sit
outside a package box, but their connectors should not obscure the main relationships.

This project has three types of tests:
1. *Unit tests* target the lowest-level methods and classes.
1. *Integration tests* check how multiple code units work together; the individual units are assumed to work.
1. *Hybrid tests* combine unit and integration testing. These tests check both the individual units and how they work together.
Test names describe the operation, scenario and expected outcome. Read the fixture setup first: each `@BeforeEach`
or `@TempDir` establishes the starting roster and isolates saved files from a real installation. An assertion on the
displayed list checks the view; it does not by itself establish that the complete roster or saved JSON is correct.
| Area | Useful starting points | What the checks establish |
| Command syntax and escaping | `TrackFlowParserTest`, `ArgumentTokenizerTest`, `ParserRobustnessTest` | Accepted/rejected input, one-time slash decoding, and unchanged state after rejection |

| Search and indexed commands | `PersonContainsKeywordsPredicateTest`, `FilterCommandTest`, `SortCommandTest` | Broad OR versus scoped AND, replacement of filters, and indexes in the displayed order |
| Identity and saved records | `PersonTest`, `DuplicatePersistenceTest`, `JsonSerializableRosterTest` | Duplicate identity, complete equality, and decisions after reloading |
| Save failures and startup | `LogicManagerTest`, `MainAppTest`, `StartupProcessTest` | Publication only after saving, preservation of unreadable data, and application-home paths |
| Screen placement | `WindowPlacementTest` | Bounds calculations for screens and saved preferences; actual rendering still needs manual checks |
For failure tests, check the expected exception or feedback as well as the unchanged roster, view and saved file.
For persistence tests, look for a fresh storage read or model reconstruction rather than an assertion against only
the original in-memory object. Comments explain unusual inputs, isolation decisions and regression risks; ordinary
setup and self-explanatory assertions do not need a comment on every line.

Replaces the remark of an athlete in the currently displayed list. Use remarks for general notes such as injuries,
personal bests or availability. To record which track events an athlete competes in, use [`tag`](#tagging-athletes-with-track-events-tag-untag) instead.
* `INDEX` refers to the index number shown in the displayed athlete list and must be a positive integer.
* Exactly one `r/` prefix is required. The prefix is case-insensitive.
* A new remark replaces the existing remark; remarks are not appended.
* Use an empty remark, such as `remark 1 r/`, to remove the athlete's existing remark.
* Remarks form part of the saved athlete record and remain after restarting TrackFlow.

* A successful remark update displays the full roster again and retains the current sort order.
Records which track events each athlete competes in. Events are shown as labels on the athlete's card. For other

* `tag` adds the given events to the athlete at `INDEX`. The athlete's existing events are kept.
* `untag` removes the given events from the athlete at `INDEX`.
* `INDEX` refers to the index number shown in the displayed athlete list and must be a positive integer.
* At least one `t/EVENT` is required. Give `t/` once per event to add or remove several events at once.
* An event is made of words of letters or digits, separated by a single space or a single hyphen, and can be up to
30 characters long, e.g. `100m`, `4x100m`, `Long Jump`, `110m-Hurdles`. Extra spaces between words are reduced to
one, but a hyphen cannot have spaces around it or be repeated: use `Long-Jump` or `Long Jump`, not `Long - Jump`
Letters include accented and non-English letters, e.g. `Saut-Élan`.
* Events ignore case: `100m` and `100M` are the same event. An event keeps the capitalisation it was first added with.
* Older rosters may contain alphanumeric tags longer than 30 characters. TrackFlow preserves these exactly when
loading and saving. They remain searchable and can be removed with `untag INDEX t/EXACT_NAME`, ignoring case.
The 30-character limit still applies when adding a new event with `tag`.
* If the athlete already has some of the events given to `tag`, only the new events are added and the message lists
the events that were skipped, as stored on the athlete. If the athlete already has all of them, an error is shown.
* If any event given to `untag` is not one of the athlete's events, an error is shown and **no** events are removed.
This guards against removing the wrong events because of a typo.
* A successful `tag` or `untag` displays the full roster again.

### Finding athletes across all or selected fields: `find`
Finds athletes using broad keywords, field-specific values, or both.
* Searchable fields are name, age category, phone, email, address, remark, and track events.
* Matching is case-insensitive and accepts partial values.
* Before any field prefix, each space-separated value is a keyword. An athlete is returned when at least one keyword occurs in at least one
searchable field (an `OR` search). This broad form remains useful when the field is unknown.
* Prefix a value to restrict it to one field: `n/` name, `a/` age category, `p/` phone, `e/` email, `addr/` address,
`r/` remark, or `t/` event. For example, `find n/und` searches names without matching every `Under` age category.
* When several field prefixes are given, an athlete must match **every** one (an `AND` search). For example,
`find n/avery a/Under 16` returns only athletes named like `avery` **and** in the `Under 16` category.
* Broad and field-specific criteria can be combined. An athlete is returned when at least one broad keyword matches
**or** every field-specific value matches. Each field prefix may appear at most once and cannot have an empty value.

* Broad keyword order does not matter: `find Avery Tan` and `find Tan Avery` return the same results. A prefixed value is matched as one phrase, so `find n/Avery Tan` matches that name but `find n/Tan Avery` does not. Put broad keywords before any field prefixes. Each athlete appears at most once.
* Each `find` searches the entire roster and replaces any previous `find` or `filter`. Matching athletes retain the
current displayed ordering, including any active sort, and receive indexes starting from 1. Use `list` to restore the complete roster.
* An empty or whitespace-only search is rejected and displays the accepted command format.
* `find ave` searches partial names and can return `Avery Tan`.
* `find under` searches age categories such as `Under 14` and `Under 16`.
* `find n/und` searches only names, so an athlete named `Underwood` can be found without matching age categories.
* `find t/hurdles` searches only events, returning athletes with an event such as `Hurdles` or `110m-Hurdles`.
* `find avery 9123 under` returns athletes matching any of the three keywords.
* `find n/rachel r/relay` returns only athletes whose name contains `rachel` **and** whose remark contains `relay`.
